A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RT-PCR typosinase analysis on peripheral blood is of no value in stage I-II melanoma patients but it is a valuable tool for the management of stage III patients.
RT-PCR analysis of melanoma mRNA in peripheral blood may have a prognostic value, but only if the analysis is sequential and the results are interpreted in the framework of disease stage.
RT-PCR typosinase positivity on PBMCs in stage III melanoma patients has an adverse prognostic significance only when it is detected at more than one time point during follow-up.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RT-PCR test is not a good prognostic indicator in patients with stage I and II melanoma.
RT-PCR analysis of tyrosinase in peripheral blood is a powerful predictor of outcome in melanoma patients, but the results of a single determination of tyrosinasedo not provide useful information.
the RT-PCR test is a prognostic marker only when used in sequential determinations.
